title: Lothric
snippet:
Lothric -  Dark Souls III - location - lothric_s_refusal 
 lothric_s_refusal : When the First Flame began to fade and the time came for Prince Lothric to fulfill his destiny and become a Lord of Cinder, he refused the call. After reflecting on his mentor's teachings, the state of the kingdom and the world, his accursed life, and the atrocities committed for the Flame, the prince decided to ignore his duty, refusing to continue the legacy of the Lords, and instead chose to await the Flame's death from the distance. The prince retired to the peak of Lothric Castle together with his brother Lorian with whom he shared a soul, protected by their royal guard and the exponents of the Three Pillars: Lion Knight Albert, Black Hand Kamui and Daughter of Crystal Kriemhild.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: Lothric, the younger prince, was the destined Lord of Cinder, who would sacrifice himself as fuel for the First Flame to uphold the Age of Fire. The prince, born a sickly, frail child, was nevertheless viewed as the "last hope of his line", the culmination of generations of Lothric rulers obsessed with producing worthy Champions for the Flame. For the anticipated journey of the young prince to the Kiln of the First Flame, a platinum sword was crafted and blessed with strong magic by the High Priestess, long before he was ready to fulfill his destiny. Oceiros created extensive propaganda around Lothric, not only giving him the name of the kingdom, but also building statues that depicted him with his sacred sword ready to complete his task, as well as preparing his throne at the Firelink Shrine in advance.

title: First Flame
snippet: By the time of *Dark Souls III*, many other such sacrifices, who have become posthumously known as Lords of Cinder, have given themselves to the First Flame, and the Age of Fire has persevered for many generations as a result. However, when the latest individual chosen for the honour, Prince Lothric, abandons his duty by refusing to link the fire, a desperate attempt to save the fading Flame begins. Four previous Lords of Cinder are resurrected to link the fire once more, however - aside from Ludleth of Courland - they too choose to flee their duties, forcing the Ashen One to drag them back.

title: Lothric
snippet: Aldia, the first of the Grand Archives scholars, seemingly became a private mentor to Prince Lothric. The young prince likely received his skepticism on the nature of the Age of Fire from his private tutor. The prince also demonstrated talent for sorcery, for which he did not need a medium—being the son of a deity—and learned several powerful and refined spells.

title: Lothric
snippet: When the royal family realized that Lothric would not improve from his condition, they resorted to repulsive acts in an attempt to obtain a worthy Champion for the linking: the rulers bound the souls of the two princes together with a curse. Although the exact motive behind this act is unknown, it is likely that the rulers intended for Prince Lothric to draw out some of the strength of his elder brother's soul, which could have allowed him to qualify as worthy Ash for the First Flame. It was even said that Lorian willingly submitted to the curse, even as it crippled him. The resulting Soul of the Twin Princes was one worthy of providing kindling for the First Flame, even as the princes were physically incapable of overcoming the obstacles involved in linking the Flame. Unable and unwilling to fulfill their destiny, the princes retreated to their chamber to await the end of the world.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

title: Knight Artorias
snippet: At the close of a period in the Age of Fire, The Abyss Watchers linked the First Flame, becoming Lords of Cinder. An indefinite amount of time later, the destined Lord of Cinder Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame, which led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves, to once again serve as kindling for the Flame. The Abyss Watchers refused to once again sacrifice themselves to the Flame, instead returning to Farron Keep, leaving their throne at Firelink Shrine empty.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lothric, Younger Prince: A prince brought into the world by the royal family of Lothric for the sole purpose of linking the Flame; however, his frailty, curse and suffering led him to reject his destiny.
Ashen One: An Unkindled who was resurrected in Lothric with the duty of linking of the First Flame, overcame multiple challenges and gathered the cinders of Lords of the past before gaining access to the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, the First Flame is so weakened that Lords of Cinder past are resurrected so that the embers of the First Flame inside them serve as fuel for new Linkings. Prince Lothric, who was raised to become the next Lord of Cinder, refused to Link the First Flame, while three of the resurrected Lords of Cinder refused to be used as fuel, leading to resurrection of several Unkindled in the hopes that one of them might slay the fleeting Lords of Cinder and Lothric, and Link the First Flame.

title: Farron Follower
snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. Among them the Abyss Watchers too rose from their graves, but refused to sacrifice themselves again to link the Fire, choosing to return to their Keep in Farron. However, the Followers were no longer present to cull the warriors that would become corrupted by the Abyss, consequently forcing the Watchers to do so themselves, wasting their strength to kill each other to contain the spreading corruption.

title: Vordt of the Boreal Valley
snippet: After Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Vordt was sent to Lothric with a division of Boreal Outrider Knights, with orders to keep a watchful eye over the Dancer of the Boreal Valley. Here he positioned himself to guard the main gate leading inside the city. Like other Outrider Knights, he would end up transformed by the rings of the Pontiff into a frenzied beast, causing his armor to be fused with his hide.

title: Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
The prince's decision led the system managing the linking of the Flame to resort to an emergency measure: ringing the bells and awakening the Lords of Cinder of the past from their graves, beings who had previously linked the Flame, to unite their cinders and energize the fading Flame. However, most of the awakened Lords of Cinder refused to sacrifice themselves again and returned to their lands, leaving their thrones at the Firelink Shrine empty.

The ringing of the bells would also awaken the Unkindled, who would hunt down the Lords of Cinder and bring their cinders back to Firelink Shrine. Many of these Unkindled attempted to storm the castle to slay Prince Lothric, but were all killed by the royal guards or by his brother Lorian.

title: Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: When the Unkindled One arrives before the prince, he's welcomed by a bitter comment from Lothric, naming them as nothing but another fool attempting to win his favour or to take his life. The feathers covering every corner of the room indicate that the Winged Knights had tried to reach the Prince to either persuade or kill him, but were all eliminated by the royal guards or by his brother Lorian. Lothric then watches as Lorian engages the Unkindled One in combat, who defeats the elder prince. Teleporting next to his brother's body, Lothric revives Lorian and climbs onto his back, kindling their bodies together. The brothers then fight the Unkindled One as one, but are unable to overcome their enemy and are both cut down. As he dies, Lothric warns the Unkindled One that they would remain among the accursed.

title: Primordial Serpents
snippet: Even after possibly hundreds of thousands years after the first linking of the Flame, Frampt (or other serpents affiliated with his ideology) continued to propagate the cult of the linking of the Flame; influencing kingdoms, rulers and simple Undead to continue the tradition started by Gwyn. When the First Flame drifted up to position itself on the nascent kingdom of Lothric, Frampt or other serpents affiliated with his ideology reached the city too. Over time the serpents passed on the culture of linking the Flame to the royal family of Lothric, pushing them to preserve the tradition and actively produce heirs capable of becoming Lords of Cinder. Frampt or his kin were represented in numerous statues, on par with the Three Pillars of Lothric, with elegant clothes and angel wings, showing their central role within the kingdom, considered "divine messengers". title: Deacons of the Deep
snippet: When the First Flame began to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, Aldrich was awakened from his tomb to become fuel for it again, but the Lord of Cinder refused the call. Aldrich was in fact intent on returning to Irithyll to devour Dark Sun Gwyndolin and usher the Age of the Deep, ending the Age of Fire and leaving in its place a realm of putrid and stagnant darkness. McDonnell, sharing Aldrich's ideals, cast off his white robes and replaced them with robes of deep blue. The Archdeacon gathered an army of deacons and evangelists, and abandoned the cathedral to follow the Saint of the Deep on his crusade toward Irithyll.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet: She eventually became wife to King Oceiros, the last monarch of Lothric, and supported the kingdom's desire to produce an heir worthy of linking the First Flame, giving birth first to Elder Prince Lorian, raised to become a knight, and Younger Prince Lothric, expected to become a "champion" and sacrifice himself to the Flame. However, when Prince Lothric and his brother refused to link the fading Flame and they chose to wait out the end of the Age of Fire, King Oceiros went mad in his attempt to produce an heir worthy of their sacrificial destiny. The king discovered the heretical faith of the paledrake Seath among the scholars of the Grand Archives and became convinced that a crossbreed heir would have the strength to link the Flame. Oceiros eventually became a deformed humanoid dragon and with him the queen had her youngest child, Ocelotte. After producing the potential champion, Gwynevere quietly disappeared from the kingdom of Lothric. Realizing that the Flame would soon go out

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Despite the message "Lord of Cinder Fallen" appearing when they die, the flaming state they have in the second phase, and Lothric having a throne dedicated to him in Firelink Shrine, the Twin Princes are thought to not have ever linked the flame. There are several points in the game that suggest this:
#The description of their soul implies that they never became Lords of Cinder.
#They are not shown in the opening cinematic, meaning they were not resurrected when the bell tolled, implying that Lothric never took his throne in the first place.
#Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle wishes for Lothric's soul to be saved by becoming a part of the firelinking ritual, implying again that Lothric never took his throne in the first place.
#After returning all Cinders of a Lord to their thrones, Lothric's head is the only one that still has its flesh.

title: Boreal Outrider Knight
snippet: After Prince Lothric refused to link the First Flame and his kingdom fell into ruin due to various internal problems, Sulyvahn would order a division of the Outrider Knights to reach Lothric, under the watchful eye of Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Here they would position themselves in various strategic points of the city, infiltrating the barracks of the Lothric army, the Grand Archives and the Undead Settlement located outside the walls, effectively controlling the places of command and movement of the kingdom.

title: Ludleth of Courland
snippet:
Sometime before or after linking the Flame, Ludleth was exiled from his country. He then collaborated with Lothric, where he ensured that all Fire Keepers to come would be deprived of their eyes, to prevent them from observing a future without the First Flame. The original eyes were hidden in a version of the Firelink Shrine on the verge of sinking into darkness, where the First Flame was all but extinguished.

Ludleth eventually linked the First Flame, taking pride in sacrificing himself of his own volition and convinced that, if in life he had been only a pygmy, in death he would have been celebrated as a true Lord. However, he also seems to express remorse for his actions, asking to be forgiven.

title: Lothric
snippet: In the beginning, the first Fire Keeper had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a barren plane of endless darkness. Acting to ward off an Age of Dark, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition of Courland, rose to the challenge of becoming a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Despite his feeble appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Lord, something for which he himself expresses remorse, asking to be forgiven. Ludleth was exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric to ensure that the Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes, as well as all future maidens, to prevent them from observing a future without the Flame. The original eyes were sealed away in an enigmatic instance of Firelink Shrine, where the First Flame had all but gone out.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In *Dark Souls III*, countless beings have prolonged the Age of Fire, preventing its end and holding off the coming of the Age of Dark. By the time the game begins, there are countless Lords of Cinder - those who successfully linked the First Flame before - and even more Unkindled who were unsuccessful. Eventually the one anointed to next link the Flame (and indeed, who was born for that very purpose), Prince Lothric, rejected the idea that the Age of Fire should be prolonged any further and instead desired to end what he called the "fire-linking curse." A contingency plan was then activated, in which previous Lords of Cinder were resurrected in hopes that they, who had linked the First Flame before, might do so again. However, by this time, the world that had been created during the Age of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. As a result of the prolonging of the current Age, the act of which seemingly constituted a rejection of the natural order, the material world

title: Lothric
snippet: As the kingdom of Lothric found itself managing the system of Firelinking,**** coupled with their subscription to the Way of Blue faith, it inevitably came into contact with Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. Ruled by Gwyndolin, the king of the gods, Irithyll and Lothric recognized a common ground in their Firelinking legacy, as well as their faith which venerated the moon god. Soon after, the two kingdoms established diplomatic relations: the scholars and knights of Lothric would travel to Irithyll, and Lothric knights would adopt crossbows that used lightning bolts produced by the giant blacksmiths of Anor Londo. The Boreal Valley also became a place of pilgrimage for the knights of Lothric, who sought to reach the residence of their patron deity in Archdragon Peak through meditation.

title: Lothric
snippet:
The relations between the two realms soon blossomed into an alliance, formalized by the incorporation of the sword of Lothric, a symbol of that realm, into the insignia of the Blades of the Darkmoon, the predecessors of the Blue Sentinels and the Way of Blue. In practice, the unification of cultural and religious symbols of the kingdoms allowed the usage of transport demons by those bearing the banner of Lothric.

Now in possession of the knowledge provided by the primordial serpents and the ancient gods of Anor Londo, the kingdom of Lothric developed its role in the linking of the Flame, building the Firelink Shrine just outside the city walls, neighbouring the Royal Gardens, in order to guarantee safe and regulated passage to the Kiln of the First Flame. The shrine would once again accept Fire Keepers who assisted Champions that aspired to link the Flame, drawing out the strength of the souls they acquired to aid them in their journey.

Before Lorian embraced his brother's curse, he was a knight who single-handedly slayed the demon prince, but the victory eternally scorched his sword with flame.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : Lothric and Lorian are the sons of Oceiros, King of Lothric and Gwynevere, Queen of Lothric and consequently the princes of the kingdom of Lothric.

Lorian, the crown prince, received the ancient brass armor handed down by the royal family, complete with a crown patterned with flame, a symbol of the kingdom's tradition of Firelinking. Lorian was raised as a knight and proved his incredible prowess on the battlefield, leading a war against the remnants of the Chaos Demons, even capturing some of them to serve as slaves for Lothric. Lorian went on to face the Demon Prince, defeating him single-handedly in a battle that eternally scorched his greatsword with the flame of chaos burned his legs and stained his armor black.

title: Demon (lore)
snippet: Like humanity and the Gods of Anor Londo of old, the demons seek to rekindle the Flame of Chaos to preserve their race. A Demon Prince, a champion of their race, challenged Prince Lorian of Lothric, only to be defeated and retreat without his memory of the flames. No longer able to pursue the rekindling of the Chaos Flame, the demon race was condemned to extinction; as time went on, even the few remaining demons all but lacked any trace of the flame within; one such lost demon, reduced to little more than a wood and stone golem, served as a gatekeeper of Lothric.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. Among them was Aldrich who, like the other exhumed Lords, had no intention of sacrificing himself again, as his reflections on the state of the world had led him to understand that an Age of the Deep would soon arrive, motivating him to devour the gods themselves, in order to erode their hold on the Flame and accelerate the coming of his vision. Gathering an army of deacons from the Cathedral of the Deep led by Archdeacon McDonnell, Aldrich would march on Irithyll, intent on capturing Anor Londo to devour the king of the gods himself. However, he would find his way blocked by Sulyvahn and his knights, as the Pontiff had no intention of relinquishing the source of his control over the city and the Way of White so easily. From the ensuing battle Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and defeating

title: Gertrude
snippet: Some of Gertrude's knights possibly attempted to reach the chambers of Prince Lothric to either kill him and prevent any Unkindled from recovering his Cinders, or convert him to have him help usher an Age of Dark; their attempts were unsuccessful as any intruders were killed by his brother Lorian. The room of the bossfight of Lothric and Lorian is covered by large, white feathers, the only creatures known to possess such wings and that could come so far into the prince's chambers being the Winged Knights and the Knights of Gertrude. The presence of a large number of Lothric knights and battle-scarred barricades before the prince's chamber, directly facing the structures presided over by the Winged Knights, also suggests a recent fight between the two groups.

title: Dark Sun Gwyndolin
snippet: her from the world and holding her hostage, unable to hear any news of her brother. Afterwards Sulyvahn took Gwyndolin himself hostage, locking him up in the old cathedral, cementing his position as Pontiff, the "voice of god", to reign through his figure, while also preventing unwanted foreign interventions.\n\nAs the First Flame began to fade Prince Lothric, who had been raised from birth to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to do so, leading the kingdom of Lothric to resurrect four dead Lords of Cinder from their graves to once again be used as fuel. Among them was Aldrich, once a cleric of Irithyll turned cannibal and saint of his own faith, who had transformed into an abysmal monstrosity due to his immeasurable hunger for humans that had made him "worthy" of linking the Flame. Like most of the resurrected Lords of Cinder, Aldrich had no intention of sacrificing himself anew, as he had come to believe that an "Age of the Deep" should come and replace the Age of Fire, motivating him

title: Timeline
snippet:
This event leads to the creation of Gundyr's ballad, staining the reputation of the Royal Family for all years to come
The civilization of Lothric comes to consider the Primordial Serpents as divine messengers, who with their advice guide the king to follow the will of the gods
Lothric culture evolves around the ritual of linking the fire, focusing on the duty of sacrifice for the royal family, the army and the population
As the centuries passed, the population and the number of graves for those who sought to link the fire increased, a larger altar was built outside the city walls
The kingdom of Lothric, as the epicenter of the First Flame, becomes the region towards which other parts of the world converge due to stagnation
The Lothric army abandons the old weapons and armor built for hunting dragons and employs more traditional protection
An old armor of the ancient dragonslayers remains as a monument near the city barracks

title: Angel
snippet: As the pilgrims of Londor were sent to Lothric with the objective to die some of them died and turned into "angels". One day one of them managed to visit Gertrude, the holy maiden of Gwynevere, Queen of Lothric and it revealed to her a truth capable of manifesting pillars of light together with a heretic tale. The holy maiden was convinced by this enlightenment and began to spread the worship of those she considered "divine messengers". However this faith was viewed as heresy in Lothric, as it opposed the worship of the ancient gods and the duty to continue linking the First Flame and was consequently unrecognized by any of the Three Pillars that govern the realm, leading to a civil war inside the walls of Lothric between the Winged Knights that followed Gertrude's faith and the Angels and those still loyal to the Pillars.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: of Fire had become a twisted shadow of its former self. As a result of the prolonging of the current Age, the act of which seemingly constituted a rejection of the natural order, the material world had become irreparably corrupted, and all lands from all previous points in time had begun to converge upon a single point: the Kingdom of Lothric. Upon reviving and seeing what had become of the world they had fought to protect, the Lords of Cinder, too, rejected the linking of the Flame and refused to sit upon their thrones. Aldrich, one of the Lords of Cinder, decided not to take his throne after experiencing visions of the deep sea and its inevitable coming.

title: Oceiros, the Consumed King
snippet: Oceiros created immense propaganda around Lothric, not only giving him the name of the kingdom, but also building statues that depicted him with his sacred sword ready to complete his task, as well as preparing his throne at the Firelink Shrine in advance. In a betrayal of the hopes placed in him, Lothric remained a sick and shriveled child from birth into adulthood, never even growing out of his baby clothes, which remained his only clothing throughout his life and were blessed to at least try to keep him healthy. In his youth, Aldia, the first of the Grand Archives scholars, became his mentor in secret, a likely influence on the young and impressionable prince, with whom he would have imparted his skepticism on the nature of the Age of Fire.

title: Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight
snippet: In the final days of Lothric, the citizens of the kingdom forgot even the miracles of the goddess of sunlight, and ended up recounting childish but earnest stories to try to recall her blessings and the back of her figure, as the last image of their queen before she left.

title: Cathedral Knight
snippet: lore : These order of knights was well-known for their impressive strenght and mighty dimensions. They were, in fact, the personal guard of King Oceiros of Lothric, and most likely the personal guard of Lothric's kings. As a proof of this, not only other identical knights can be found in in the Consumed King's Garden, with the only difference of the former ones wearing blue robes and tunics, as the distinct colour of the Royal Family's Guard in Lothric, but their own shields are decorated with "an emblem of an old king of Lothric". This testifies the strong connection and alliance that linked Lothric with the Way of White and the government of Anor Londo (Irithyll) before Prince Lothric renouced his role as Lord of Cinder and despised the link of fire, but it also tells about how great and spreaded was the concern of the Cathedral getting increasingly swallowed and corrupted by the Depths: so much that Lothric's king decided to send a regiment of his personal guard to keep the order

title: Gods
snippet:
Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince, oldest two sons of Oceiros and Gwynevere when the latter was Queen of Lothric. Lorian was raised to inherit his father's throne, while Lothric was raised to become a Lord of Cinder; however, Lothric was born frail and weak, leading Lorian to join their souls together in an attempt to assist his brother. Ultimately, Lothric refused to Link the First Flame altogether.
Ocelotte, last child of Gwynevere and Oceiros. His father attempted to turn Ocelotte into a "child of dragons".
Shira, Knight of Filianore, daughter of the dragon Seath and the relative of Gwyn he married, sworn to protecting the slumber of Gwyn's child Filianore.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - unkindled_resurrected_to_supplant_lothric_younger_prince_prince_lothric 
 unkindled_resurrected_to_supplant_lothric_younger_prince_prince_lothric : The Ashen One, who eventually decides the fate of the First Flame.
Anri of Astora, who was one of only two children to have escaped the clutches of Aldrich, their cannibalistic father. Aldrich, as a Lord of Cinder, had been resurrected in the hopes of replacing Lothric; Anri in their second life aims to slay him, to fulfill their duty as a Lordseeker as well as to avenge their devoured siblings.

title: Flame of Chaos
snippet:
By the events of *Dark Souls III*, however, the flame is dying and the Demons are as well. The Stray Demon lacks any flame whatsoever.

Though it was not successful in replacing the First Flame, it functions similarly to it, as Demons can become powerful enough to "link" it and rekindle it when it dies out. The chosen one for this task was the Demon Prince, whose will is within all Demonkind, but his defeat at the hands of Prince Lorian of Lothric, and later the Ashen One, left the demon race without a champion, rendering them extinct.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - plot 
 plot : By the times of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, the destined Lord of Cinder of his generation, has refused to link the First Flame. This led to the resurrection of four Lords of Cinder of the past, whose conjoined, withered embers could kindle the First Flame in Lothric's stead. Aldrich, Saint of the Deep; Yhorm the Giant, the Abyss Watchers, and Ludleth of Courland were expected to sacrifice themselves as kindling once again. When all Lords except Ludleth rejected this duty, the Unkindled too were resurrected as a last resort, who were fated to seek out the Lords (including Prince Lothric) and bring them back to their thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once the cinders of the Lords were restored to their thrones, an Unkindled champion would be bestowed the embers of the First Flame that remained within their cinders, and finally sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to complete their journey.

title: Gods
snippet:
Gwynevere, Princess of Sunlight was the Queen of Lothric and conceiving Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince, the younger son destined to link the First Flame. However, after Lothric refused to fulfill his duty, King Oceiros became obsessed with the power of dragons . Gwynevere granted his wish for an heir of divine and draconic blood and gave birth to her last children Ocelotte, however she later abandoned the kingdom of Lothric and quietly disappeared .

Filianore, Gwyn's last daughter, still remains in the Ringed City, asleep to keep the city outside the flow of time and space. Shira, Knight of Filianore, daughter of Seath, continues to remain at her side, defending the princess's sleep and maintaining control over the noble Pygmy family.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The **Ashen One,** also referred to as the **Champion of Ash** or **the Unkindled One,** is the playable character and the protagonist of *Dark Souls III*.

The title of Ashen One is given to the player by the Fire Keeper of Firelink Shrine. The Ashen One is an Unkindled, an Undead who failed to link the First Flame and became ash, who has been raised from their grave, and is tasked with a journey to defeat four Lords of Cinder and return them to their thrones, since the link of the Flame is threatened and the Lords refuse to serve as its fuel once again.

title: Age of Fire
snippet:
Age of Fire -  Dark Souls - storyline - description 
 description : **WARNING: This entire page lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations to be considered even useful**

The Age of Fire first began after Gwyn and the other Lords defeated the Everlasting Dragons which ended the Age of Ancients. The Age of Fire was unnaturally prolonged when Gwyn sacrificed himself to kindle the First Flame.

When the Chosen Undead talks to Kingseeker Frampt, he will tell them that they are destined to succeed Gwyn. Should the player choose to kindle the First Flame upon the defeat of Gwyn, they will sacrifice themselves as Gwyn did, thus delaying the Age of Dark once more.

Such a routine of kindling the First Flame repeats itself for generations to come, until the time of Prince Lothric, when the prolonging of the fire proves futile.

title: Witch of Izalith
snippet: Ages after her Lord Soul was used to link the First Flame, Izalith's very name was lost. In the region of Drangleic, only few remained who remembered her—only that she was the mother of pyromancy, and that she was devoured by her chaos flame. However, some remnants of her soul manifested again in Drangleic, continuing to exert their influence on the region.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Vendrick fled the Castle through the King's Passage never to return, fearing Nashandra's wickedness. He left the Looking Glass Knight behind him, ready to expunge those who would challenge him, forever true to his original command, as the first line of defense against those who would attempt to pursue the runaway king into the Undead Crypt. The king took with him only a handful of Royal Soldiers and the faithful Sir Velstadt, and found refuge in the Shrine of Amana. Vendrick was initially intent on reaching the Throne of Want and link the First Flame but in the end the king understood that if he did so, Nashandra would have gained an easy access to the throne connected to the Flame. Vendrick thus decided to free himself from his soul, abandoning it among the ruins, to descend even deeper into the Undead Crypt. Here, left alone, he isolated himself in a secluded room wearing only his robes, crown, sword and his ring. Overcome by nihilism, Vendrick was consumed by the curse and soon

title: Untended Graves
snippet:
Untended Graves -  Dark Souls III - location - lore 
 lore : This location is sealed away from the eye of everyone, hidden in secret within the deepest parts of Lothric's castle: it shows a time, in the past of Lothric, when the Fire almost faded completely, and with the light nearly eradicated, time has stagnated to the point where past, present and future co-exist. That is the reason why Gundyr is not yet "Iudex", "judge of the ash": Gundyr was a champion who "came too late" and was "greeted by a shrine without fire, and a bell that would not toll.". He was bested by an unknown warrior and became the sheath of a Coiled Sword, in the hopes that someday, the first flame would be linked once more.

title: Sister Friede
snippet:
With Elfriede at the helm, the Sable Church developed dark miracles, forged specialized weaponry, and trained knights unflinchingly loyal to their cause. The influence of the Sable Church would extend beyond Londor and into other realms via Londor Pale Shades, assassins and knights who served the interests of the Church abroad. At some point, Sir Vilhelm would come under the employ of the three sisters of the Church. He was especially loyal to Elfriede, becoming her steadfast follower and cold-blooded hangman.

Elfriede eventually departed Londor to attempt to link the First Flame. It is uncertain whether she intended to usurp the Flame, realizing Kaathe's vision of an Age of Dark, or wholly abandoned Londor to link the Flame for another purpose. Regardless, she was unable to withstand the Flame's power, and was burned to Ash.

title: Ludleth of Courland
snippet: When the link of fire was threatened, the Lords of Cinder would be exhumed from their graves to once again serve as kindling for the First Flame. Ludleth was among those resurrected; though unlike the other three Lords, he accepted the call, and took up his throne at Firelink Shrine to await his fate.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet:
Gwyn, Lord of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : The remnants of the will and power of Gwyn, as the first one to ever link the First Flame, would emerge as part of the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who have linked themselves to the First Flame throughout history, thus creating a hollowed-out entity possessing all the abilities of the previous Champions.

The powers of Gwyn would manifest when the Soul of Cinder was challenged by an aspiring Champion; acting as the Flame's last line of defense within the Kiln, the Soul of Cinder fought to either test the might of one who would link the Flame, or to protect it from a would-be betrayer or usurper.

title: The Deep
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their humanity, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder—just for his strength, without regard for his morality. Now left to indulge in his perversions so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. Aldrich, despite his unbridled hedonism, still decided to follow his ideals on the Age of Fire as a cleric and, when the time came, he sacrificed himself on the Flame to prolong its life.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their very essence, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder just for his strength, without any consideration for his morality or how he acquired his power. Now left to indulge in his every perversion so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. Aldrich, despite his unbridled hedonism, still decided to follow his ideals on the Age of Fire as a cleric and, when the time came, he sacrificed himself on the Flame to prolong its life.

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet: It was not chance that bound him to this fate, however: The one who had charged him with his duty had also condemned him to eternal service from the beginning. Imprisoned, Gundyr was defeated by an unknown warrior and became sheath to a coiled sword. Transformed into an indestructible golem, he became the ritual test of strength for those who would attempt to link the First Flame after him. Over time an arena complete with stands was built around his remains, in which the now Iudex Gundyr would "judge" those who aspired to become Lords.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - lead 
 lead : The **Unkindled** or are "nameless, accursed Undead" who tried to link the First Flame and become Lords of Cinder, being mighty enough to reach the Kiln of the First Flame but ultimately perishing there, their quest ending in failure.

title: Demon Prince
snippet:
Demon Prince -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Chaos Flame, like the First Flame that it was unable to replace, is capable of being rekindled by a champion demon of vast power. Such a so-called "prince" went to face Lorian, eldest son of the Lothric royal family, and was defeated in combat. But the race of demons shares memory with each other, and those that remembered the power and determination of the Demon Prince share in this essence, so that even the last demon alive can rekindle the Chaos Flame.

At the end of the Age of Fire, reality has partially collapsed onto itself, gathering all lands onto one point of convergence. At the bottom of a large tree rest two demons, the last demons by that time, and the last one to survive shall be reborn as the Demon Prince.

title: Crown of the Great Lord
snippet:
Crown of the Great Lord -  Dark Souls - armor - description 
 description : Crown of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, who linked the First Flame.

Lord Gwyn, bearer of the ultimate soul, divided that power among his great clan before linking the flame. But he did keep his crown, perhaps to preserve a symbol of the monarch, for its actual power had fully subsided.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Soul of Cinder: A deific manifestation of the souls of all those who have linked themselves to the First Flame through history.
Yhorm the Giant: A giant humanoid, king of the Profaned Capital, who linked the First Flame in an attempt to save his city from the Profaned Flame.
Ludleth of Courland: A small pygmy from Courland and a student of the art of transposition: the process of extracting and coalescing the essence of souls to gain incredible powers.
Abyss Watchers: A legion of Undead soldiers tasked with fighting the Abyss wherever it takes shape, united in their souls by the wolf blood of Artorias to link the First Flame and do their duty one last time.
Aldrich, Saint of the Deep: A cleric from Irithyll of the Boreal Valley who took pleasure in devouring humans, eating so much that his body became a sludge of darkness and was made to link the First Flame for his strength.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The are characters who have linked the First Flame throughout the history of the *Dark Souls* universe.

To "link the First Flame" is to reach it, be powerful enough to withstand its power, and rekindle the flame anew; it is done in order to stop the First Flame from withering out and dying, a process that occurs naturally over time and would mean both the end of the Age of Fire and the coming of an Age of Dark. To attempt to link the flame, one must typically reach the kiln built around the First Flame and defeat the empty husk of the previous Lords of Cinders guarding it against those not worthy of its power.

title: Braille Divine Tome of Lothric
snippet:
Braille Divine Tome of Lothric -  Dark Souls III - item - description 
 description : A sacred braille tome from Lothric, filled with miracles for use by knights.

Give to a storyteller to learn Lothric miracles.

It is said that no paladin inside Lothric castle could fall, owing to the divine protection they enjoyed.

title: Braille Divine Tome of Lothric
snippet:
Braille Divine Tome of Lothric -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : Given to Irina of Carim will unlock the following miracles:
Blessed Weapon
Bountiful Light

title: Braille Divine Tome of Lothric
snippet:
Braille Divine Tome of Lothric -  Dark Souls III - item - lead 
 lead : The **Braille Divine Tome of Lothric** (ロスリックの点字聖書) is a key item in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Braille Divine Tome of Lothric
snippet:
Braille Divine Tome of Lothric -  Dark Souls III - item - notes 
 notes : This item can theoretically be obtained extremely early, before even meeting Irina of Carim, though doing this requires killing Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle, defeating the Dancer of the Boreal Valley, and traversing the Dragon Barracks.

title: Braille Divine Tome of Lothric
snippet:
Braille Divine Tome of Lothric -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : The tome is located in Lothric Castle. From the Dragon Barracks bonfire the player can proceed through the area until they reach the Dragonslayer Armour fog wall. Before entering, head to the left, dropping down to the platform containing one of the Lothric Wyverns. The tome is in the room behind it.
